item.title: Miami opens its post-Carson Beck era against Stanford in a key college football week 1 matchup
item.description: Miami Hurricanes open their season with just eight returning starters and new quarterback Darian Mensah facing a Stanford team already warmed up.
item.content:encoded:
Can you believe we are already here? Friday of Week 1 of College Football. Do you even know what is on the horizon for us? Tonight, there are a handful of games, after we had a decent slate yesterday. Tomorrow, a full day of the gridiron commences. Then, the NFL comes next week, and we are on the verge of having football every week until basically February. I. Can’t. Wait.

The Miami Hurricanes come into this game as the seventh-ranked team in the nation and are coming off of their best season in years. They came this close to upsetting Indiana in the College Football Playoff National Championship, before losing 27-21. The team did have some questionable losses, which have been their downfall over the past few seasons. They lost to Louisville at home in a game that was very bad for Carson Beck. They also lost on the road to SMU. However, they were outstanding in the playoffs.

This year will face some challenges, of course. They no longer have Beck under center, so that’s going to be an adjustment at the very least. The team has Darian Mensah coming from Duke, where he threw 34 touchdowns and just six interceptions with almost 4,000 passing yards. That’s impressive work. He seems to be mostly a pocket passer and doesn’t rely on his legs to extend plays, so the offensive line will need to give him time, especially early as he builds rapport with his team.

Stanford already has a game under its belt and has a bit of an advantage over the Hurricanes because the Cardinal is used to game speed. That doesn’t always mean anything, but it is at least worth noting and considering. The Cardinal beat the Hawai’i Rainbow Warriors last week, but that game was significantly closer than you would’ve expected given the final score. Stanford won 37-27, but this was after blowing a 16-point lead. They were down four with about 3:12 before scoring a touchdown and returning a fumble for another score.

Overall, the team looked pretty good outside half of the fourth quarter. New quarterback Davis Warren was 22-for-34 with 310 yards and one touchdown. I think what I liked most about his game is that there were nine different receivers hauling in passes. Micah Ford, their running back, racked up 100 yards on 25 carries, which isn’t overly efficient, but still pretty solid. His three touchdowns were a positive look.

item.title: Canadian fan disses Trump's Lake America renaming at FIBA Women's World Cup with sign
item.description: A Canadian fan's sign at the FIBA Women's World Cup directly challenged President Donald Trump's executive order renaming Lake Ontario as Lake America.
item.content:encoded:
A Canadian fan attending Team USA’s game at the FIBA World Cup on Friday has taken aim at President Donald Trump.

The fan brought a sign to the game that expressed her apparent displeasure with Trump’s recent executive order renaming Lake Ontario as Lake America.

On one side of the sign, the fan wrote, "Lake America?" in blue marker. The fan then turned the sign around to express her disdain, writing "Lake Ontario!!" in red marker.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Trump’s executive order to rename the Great Lake comes amid a trade war with Canada.

"The Lake of America was something I've been thinking about for a long time, actually. As you know, we took something called the Gulf of Mexico — we changed it — and now it's very routinely the Gulf of America," Trump said in the Oval Office last month.

The executive order called the United States the greatest protector of the Great Lakes.

CAITLIN CLARK POSTS DOUBLE-DOUBLE AS TEAM USA OPENS FIBA WOMEN'S WORLD CUP WITH BLOWOUT WIN OVER CHINA

"Without the security and investment provided by the United States, this freshwater system would not be open for shipping, recreation, and responsible use to the same extent as it is today."

Trump directed Interior Secretary Doug Burgum and the department to reflect the name change in the Geographic Names Information System. While the name change may be embraced in the United States, it clearly is not resonating north of the border.

While the Canadian fan expressed her displeasure with the name change, she did get to see the United States open the FIBA Women’s World Cup with a dominant win over China.

The United States won 94-61, with Caitlin Clark recording a double-double in her senior international debut with 14 points and 11 assists in 25 minutes off the bench. Paige Bueckers and Rhyne Howard also had 14 points apiece the win for the United States.

Fox News' Louis Casiano contributed to this report.

item.title: Fake patient portal scam can steal your login and infect your PC
item.description: MyChart phishing emails mimic real patient portal alerts with fake lab results and malware tricks that target Windows users across the country.
item.content:encoded:
If you have ever checked a lab result or sent your doctor a message online, you may already know MyChart. It is a widely used patient portal from Epic that hospitals and medical practices use to give patients online access to health information and care teams.

That growing reliance on patient portals caught the attention of Mary M. She recently wrote to us after hearing from her primary care physician, or PCP, and several specialists about moving more of their patient communication online.

"I just got a lot of updates from my PCP and specialist doctors saying they are moving toward this, but they are already compromised!! I think this is a topic for you!"

Mary raised a concern many patients may share as they hear about scams targeting MyChart users. There is an important point to clear up. The warnings reviewed here describe criminals impersonating MyChart through phishing campaigns. They do not report a breach of the MyChart platform itself.

MEDICARE AND SOCIAL SECURITY SCAMS: WARNING SIGNS AND TIPS

Epic has documented scams that copy the MyChart experience to steal login details. One version can also push malware onto Windows computers. Here's how the scam works and how to protect yourself before a fake MyChart alert catches you off guard.

Missed CyberGuy LIVE? Watch the Protect Your Money replay

Our free CyberGuy LIVE class, Protect Your Money From Today’s Biggest Threats, has ended, but you can still watch the full replay and download our financial protection checklist. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson walks you through five simple ways to help defend yourself against AI scams, fraud, identity theft and financial hacks. You’ll learn how to set up bank alerts, strengthen your account logins, protect your phone number, freeze your credit and help secure your retirement savings against unauthorized transfers. No technical experience is needed.

Get the free replay and checklist now at CyberGuyLive.com

This one caught my attention because the warnings are coming from several credible sources at nearly the same time. Penn Medicine said on Aug. 26, 2026, that it was seeing a nationwide scam involving emails and text messages made to look like they came from MyChart. Then, on Aug. 28, Pennsylvania Attorney General Dave Sunday warned consumers about another MyChart impersonation scam involving a bogus Medicare Kit.

Epic has also detailed two phishing campaigns its security team investigated this summer. Put all of that together, and you can see why I want you to be especially careful with unexpected MyChart messages right now.

The tricky part is that many of us are already used to getting legitimate emails about appointments or new test results. A fake MyChart alert can land right alongside the real ones, and scammers are counting on you reacting before you take a closer look.

One campaign starts with a message that looks routine. Epic says the email carries MyChart branding and tells the recipient, "Your recent results are ready."

The button inside the email leads to a fake sign-in page. According to Epic, scammers copied code from the real MyChart site, which helps the page look convincing.

The bogus page asks for an email address and password. If you enter them, the scammers can capture those credentials. Then the attack gets more aggressive.

After the victim signs in, the fake site displays a made-up medical record. Epic says one version shows a pop-up claiming an "AI-powered review" found critical patterns in blood work.

That is a powerful pressure tactic. A warning about your health can be much harder to ignore than an ordinary phishing message.

Epic says real critical results come from your care team rather than a website pop-up. The fake chart then claims you need to complete a human verification step before seeing more information.

This part should stop you immediately. Epic says the site instructs Windows users to press the Windows key and R, paste content from the clipboard and press Enter. Those steps open the Windows Run box and execute a command the website placed on the clipboard. According to Epic, following those instructions installs malware.

Epic also saw an August 2026 version with an "Unlock Full Report & See Diagnosis" button. Clicking it downloaded a Windows file called Full_Analysis_Report.exe. The page then coached the victim through bypassing the computer's security warning. Your medical results should appear inside MyChart. A patient portal should never require you to download a Windows program to reveal a diagnosis.

FAKE PASSWORD-MANAGER ALERTS COULD PUT YOUR VAULT AT RISK

The second campaign uses a different hook. Epic says scammers sent fake emails telling people they had been selected for a "2026 Medicare Health Kit." Penn Medicine has also warned about messages advertising a free "MyChart Medicare Kit" or "Senior Health Package." MyChart does not run giveaways.

After someone clicks, Epic says the link can pass through unrelated advertising sites before reaching a fake MyChart-branded survey. A countdown clock pushes the victim to move quickly. Eventually, the site says the kit costs $0 but asks for a shipping fee. Before payment, it collects personal information. The final page asks for credit card details. Epic says no kit ships.

Patients already expect electronic messages from doctors and hospitals. A real test-result notification may show up on the same day as a fake one. Scammers can copy that familiar routine. They can also use fear to shorten the amount of time you spend checking a message.

If a fake portal hints at a serious health problem, your first instinct may be to find out what happened. That is why opening the portal independently can make such a difference. We recently covered another healthcare scam that uses fake QR codes around medical settings. Those codes can send patients to bogus sites asking for patient portal credentials or Medicare information. The MyChart campaign follows the same basic idea. The scammer borrows trust from a healthcare service you already recognize.

A few simple steps can help you slow things down before an urgent-looking message leads you to the wrong place.

If an email says a new result is waiting, avoid using the button inside the message. Open the MyChart app directly. You can also use a saved bookmark or start from your healthcare provider's official website. Epic says each healthcare organization can have its own MyChart URL. You can use MyChart.org to find your provider's official portal.

Do not rely on the sender name alone. An email can display "MyChart" while coming from an unrelated address. Look at the full address and compare it with previous legitimate messages from your healthcare provider. If anything feels off, contact your provider through a phone number or website you already trust.

MyChart says it will never tell you to use keyboard shortcuts or run a command to verify, fix or unlock your account. A website asking you to open the Windows Run box should be an immediate warning sign. Close the page.

MyChart supports two-step verification (2FA). The extra check can help protect your account if someone gets your password. Depending on your setup, you can verify your login through a code or an authenticator app. MyChart also supports passkeys, which can reduce your reliance on a reusable password.

Avoid reusing a password from another important account. A password manager can create and store a strong password for you. If a phishing site captures one password, reuse can turn one stolen login into a much larger problem.

The malware part of this scam shows why strong security protection still has a role. Strong antivirus software can help warn you about malicious downloads or suspicious websites. Keep Windows and your browser updated too. For more ways to recognize suspicious email, see our guide on how to spot and prevent phishing attacks in your inbox.

If a message claims a serious result needs immediate attention, do not let the urgency decide what you click. Open the official MyChart app yourself or call your provider using a number you already trust. Epic specifically warns that real critical results come from your care team rather than a scary website pop-up.

Scammers can make phishing messages more convincing when they already know details such as your phone number, home address, age or family connections. A data removal service can help remove some of that information from people-search sites and data brokers. It will not stop a fake MyChart message from reaching you, but it can give scammers less personal information to work with when they try to make a message feel legitimate. Check out my top picks for data removal services and get a free scan to find out if your personal information is already out on the web by visiting CyberGuy.com.

Epic says MyChart does not run giveaways. If an email promises a free Medicare kit or health package under the MyChart name, do not enter personal information or payment details.

FAKE PARTY INVITATION SCAM CAN HIJACK YOUR COMPUTER

Your next move depends on what happened after you opened the page.

Close the page. If you did not enter any information, run a command or download a file, avoid interacting with the site any further. Mark the original message as junk or phishing. Do not click an unsubscribe link inside the suspicious message.

Go to MyChart through the official app or your provider's trusted website. Change your password right away. Then review the contact information saved in your account, including your email address and phone number. If anything looks unfamiliar, contact your healthcare organization's MyChart help desk.

Call your bank or card issuer using the number printed on the card. Tell them the card information went to a fraudulent website and ask about replacing the card.

Disconnect the computer from the internet. Have the computer checked before you use it again for sensitive activity. Run a full security scan with strong antivirus software. Get my picks for the best 2026 antivirus protection winners for your Windows, Mac, Android and iOS devices at CyberGuy.com. Then change important passwords from another trusted device if you used those accounts on the affected computer.

Contact your healthcare provider and health insurer. Medical identity theft can create problems beyond a stolen password. Fraudulent activity can end up connected to your health records or insurance. We explain the warning signs and recovery steps in medical identity theft follows you into the doctor's office.

What gets me about this scam is how naturally it fits into something many of us already do. Doctors want patients using portals because they make it easier to see results and stay connected with a care team. Scammers know those messages already have our attention. I would keep using MyChart if my doctors rely on it. I would simply change how I respond to unexpected notifications. If an email says an important result is waiting, I would open the app myself rather than letting the email choose where I go. The malware trick also deserves extra attention. A website asking you to open the Windows Run box or ignore a security warning has crossed a very clear line. Close it and verify the message through your provider. The hardest part may be resisting the fear factor. A message about an abnormal medical result can make anyone move quickly. Taking a few extra seconds to open the real app could protect your patient account and your computer.

item.content:encoded:

"Nearly 3,000 New Yorkers died on 9/11; 22 years later, the death hasn't stopped. We mourn our neighbors who died that day. The hundreds of thousands who died in the wars that followed. The unknown millions injured & displaced. In their memory, we work toward a better world," Mamdani wrote on X in 2023.

Some 9/11 families have called on the socialist mayor not to attend New York City’s 9/11 commemoration after he faced backlash for interviewing Hasan Piker, who in 2019 said, "America deserved 9/11." "I guess they all just 'died' in an accident? And then you wonder why the families of 9/11 victims don’t want you at the ceremony. Stay home, Mamdani," wrote New York City council woman Inna Vernikov.

You and your buddy Piker can spend the day practicing Mandarin," said Fox News contributor and ex-NYPD officer Paul Mauro.

item.title: Washington Commanders bet on healthy Jayden Daniels to bounce back from injury-plagued 2025 season
item.description: Jayden Daniels returns healthy as the Commanders target a bounce-back season, but key roster moves and a tough NFC East raise the stakes further.
item.content:encoded:
Head coach Dan Quinn is entering his third season in the District, and dynamic quarterback Jayden Daniels is looking to reclaim his star trajectory; Washington is aiming to prove that last season’s sub-.500 stumble was purely a health-related fluke and that they are ready to contend once again in the NFC East.

The Commanders suffered through an injury-ravaged 2025 campaign, dropping 10 of their final 12 games to finish 5–12 and missing the postseason entirely. Jayden Daniels was limited to just seven starts while battling persistent injuries, missing 10 full games and forcing Washington to lean heavily on backup signal-callers. With an offense operating at half-strength and a defense that surrendered over 6.0 yards per play, Washington finished near the bottom of the league in DVOA and lost quite a few one-possession heartbreakers.

SUPER BOWL CHAMPION JOE THEISMANN EXPLAINS WHY COMMANDERS ARE POISED TO BOUNCE BACK FROM DISAPPOINTING SEASON

The headlining move came along the front seven, as Washington signed pass rusher Charles Omenihu to bolster the edge rotation and brought in former Michigan safety Sonny Styles via the draft to inject athletic versatility into the secondary. The front office also re-signed key interior trench pieces, keeping offensive guard Sam Cosmi locked up alongside defensive tackle Daron Payne, while adding offensive line depth with veteran additions to protect Daniels.

item.content:encoded:
WWE NXT star Kelani Jordan added another line to her already impressive pro wrestling resume just four years after she initially signed with the company and reported to the Performance Center.

She was the first NXT women’s North American champion, she won the Total Nonstop Action Wrestling (TNA) Knockouts Championship and, on Sunday at Heatwave, she defeated Kendal Grey to win the NXT Women’s Championship for the first time in her first opportunity.

OutKick Dropkick asked Jordan in a recent interview what the accolades meant to her.

"It feels great. Also, it's a good reminder to, like, whenever there's moments where I'm like maybe down or feel like, oh no, I'm like kind of like plateauing or shoot, like what's happening, I think it's a good reminder to like, hey, you were the first ever North American champion, you were a TNA Knockouts champion, now you're the NXT women's champion.

"It just allows me to take a moment to reflect and be like, hey, like you're very talented and you're good. Like you don't have these titles for no reason or had those titles for no reason. So, I think it's a great reminder that Kelani Jordan is a force to be reckoned with."

Over the course of the year, Jordan has demanded respect from fans and the rest of the women’s locker room. She said in May she was better than all the women that were called up to Raw and SmackDown after WrestleMania 42.

Now, Jordan has the belt to prove it.

"Yes, absolutely," she said when asked about whether she’s earned the respect of her peers. "I mean, of course, I know there's a target on my back, an even bigger one if there wasn't one already because I am the champion. But I think people know when they're in the ring with me that they're in for a tough, tough fight.

"But definitely when you have the title, you automatically get a little bit more respect. You know what I'm saying? Just because I mean it's proven in your work. You're the champion. So you have something around your waist or over your shoulder to like speak for that."

Jaida Parker was the first one to step up to Jordan on Tuesday night.

Parker is coming off a big win in a submission match against Nattie, which also took place on Heatwave. She’s certainly proved to be a worthy contender.

"Yeah, I'm not surprised that Jaida Parker came out. I had a feeling someone was going to come out, but I'm not surprised that it was her because we have a lot of history and like she said, she feels like she has a chip on her shoulder because we faced each other before.

"But I know Jada is going to bring a lot of fight. I know she's great at talking, but I'm great not only at talking, but I walk the walk. So, I am ready for Jaida's games, her tactics. She can talk, but when she's in the ring with me is, you know, talking — is that going to work?"

Jordan and Parker’s match for the NXT Women’s Championship is set for this coming Tuesday on the CW Network.

item.title: WNBA Commissioner Cathy Engelbert to retire at end of calendar year, ending controversial tenure
item.description: WNBA Commissioner Cathy Engelbert is retiring at the end of the calendar year. Englebert was the first-ever WNBA commissioner in league history, serving in the role for seven years.
item.content:encoded:
WNBA Commissioner Cathy Engelbert is retiring at the end of the calendar year. 

Engelbert was the first-ever WNBA commissioner in league history, serving in the role for seven years. The news was announced by NBA commissioner Adam Silver. 

"Cathy has presided over the WNBA through the most significant period of growth in the league’s 30-year history," Silver said in the WNBA’s statement.  "We are grateful for Cathy’s leadership and unwavering commitment to the advancement of women’s basketball."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

The timing of her retirement comes after a year full of controversy in the WNBA. Indiana Fever’s Sophie Cunningham’s comments about trans athletes in women’s sports and the treatment of Caitlin Clark have been the dominating storylines throughout this season. 

"After more than seven years at the WNBA and more than 40 total years in business, I have made the decision to retire as WNBA Commissioner," Engelbert said in a statement.  

"In 2019, I had the privilege of being appointed the league’s first commissioner and to lead a league with enormous potential yet untapped awareness and significant undervaluation.  Over the years, it has been amazing to watch WNBA players thrive and lead the massive cultural surge around women’s sports."

Under Engelbert's tenure, the league expanded from 12 to 18 teams while also overseeing the WNBA's media rights and collective bargaining agreement. While she has been highly criticized for not marketing the WNBA's superstars enough, namely Clark, the league has seen tremendous growth under Engelbert. 

In the WNBA's statement, the league said Engelbert helped oversee "increases in viewership and historic highs have been reached in digital engagement, game attendance, League Pass subscribers, merchandise sales, corporate partnership revenues and franchise valuations."

The WNBA schedule has drastically changed under Engelbert. In 2021, she introduced the WNBA's in-season Commissioner's Cup tournament. In 2025, she expanded the regular season to 44 games and announced that the WNBA would play a record-high 50 games in 2027.

The 61-year-old said she is retiring with gratitude and optimism for the WNBA's future. 

"I retire knowing we have built something bigger, stronger and more enduring than we could have imagined.  I am grateful to the WNBA and NBA team owners and staff, players, investors, fans and the powerhouse league office staff, who believed in what this league could become.  I retire with immense gratitude and tremendous optimism for the future of the WNBA, with the best yet to come," Engelbert said. 

It is not yet known who will replace her.

item.title: Boo Carter's stellar field goal block seals Colorado's stunning 14-13 road win over Georgia Tech
item.description: Boo Carter's field goal block sealed the Colorado Buffaloes' 14-13 stunner after Julian Lewis hit Charlie Williams for a late touchdown in Atlanta.
item.content:encoded:
The college football season just began in the best way for Deion Sanders and the Colorado Buffaloes.

For the Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets, it was heartbreak on the final play of Thursday night’s game in Atlanta.

Colorado pulled off a 14-13 victory on the road after Boo Carter blocked a game-winning field goal attempt by Georgia Tech from 45 yards out, stunning a sold-out crowd at Bobby Dodd Stadium and starting a wild celebration on the field for the Buffaloes.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

Carter’s heroics would’ve been nothing, though, if it wasn’t for Colorado quarterback Julian Lewis finding tight end Charlie Williams for a 20-yard touchdown with 37 seconds to go in the game.

COLORADO FOOTBALL OPENS PRACTICE TO FANS AND REPORTERS, BUT TREATS IT LIKE A CLASSIFIED PENTAGON BRIEFING

The touchdown snapped quite the drought of offense for Sanders’ squad, as the Buffaloes were able to find the end zone in the second quarter but couldn’t muster anything else until that game-winning touchdown late in the fourth.

But the Buffaloes’ defense kept them going in the game. They also blanked Georgia Tech in the third quarter and kept it a 10-7 game until Yellow Jackets kicker Aidan Birr hit a field goal to further the lead.

What should be encouraging moving forward for the Buffaloes is how dominant they were in the run game under new offensive coordinator Breanna Marion. Colorado outrushed Georgia Tech, 183-51, but they were unable to convert that positive rush attack into points.

On the other hand, Sanders and the Buffaloes will need to work on special teams despite Carter’s brilliant rush off the edge during that field goal block.

The Yellow Jackets’ only touchdown on the night was a 100-yard kickoff returned for the score by Rahkeem Smith in the second quarter. And despite the connection between Lewis and Williams with just seconds remaining, Colorado had a go-ahead field goal attempt that was blocked in the fourth quarter.

item.title: Pro Football Hall of Fame making massive overhaul of its selection process following 2026 Bill Belichick snub
item.description: The Pro Football Hall of Fame is slashing its selection committee from 50 to 28 members and eliminating the senior category in a sweeping overhaul.
item.content:encoded:
The Pro Football Hall of Fame is making massive changes to its process for picking future Hall of Famers.

The Hall says it is hoping to "improve its selection process" from one that led to the 2026 class not including former New England Patriots head coach Bill Belichick as one of its "most-deserving" candidates as a first-ballot Hall of Famer.

"The Hall continually reviews its bylaws to ensure the selection process reflects the highest standards of integrity and the magnitude of election to the Pro Football Hall of Fame," said Hall of Fame president Jim Porter. "There is no more important task at the Hall of Fame than the election of each new class."

FOOTBALL LEGEND BILL BELICHICK ADDRESSES HALL OF FAME SNUB AND WHETHER IT WAS A 'POLITICAL' DECISION

The Hall has decided to cut the number of selectors from 50 people down to 28. Of that reduced number, three will be non-voting alternates.

That means the days when every NFL team had a representative intimately tied to that team on the selection committee are over.

Some current selectors who are being removed will be asked to participate in various Hall of Fame committees.

The identity of the selectors remaining and those removed is still being decided by the Hall of Fame, according to Porter.

As some selectors are being eliminated so is the traditional system of presentation. For decades selectors presented Hall candidates to the rest of the selectors by stating a case for that person using statistics, testimony and endorsements from various respected football sources.

The entire group of selectors would then debate the pros and cons of that candidate before voting.

Under the new system, one voice from a non-selector will introduce each candidate by simply announcing his name and sharing his resume. Then the reduced group of selectors will go immediately into discussion on the merits of that candidate.

So, why is the formal presentation disappearing?

The PFHOF is trying to avoid what it calls "unintended biases" in its selection process and one way to do that is to limit the advantage some selectors have had because of their superior oratory skills over others, according to the Hall.

The categories the selection committee will now consider have been cut to three:

Player.

Coach.

Contributor.

The past splitting of players into modern-era players and senior players will end. All players from all eras not currently in the Hall of Fame will all be lumped into one category for nomination.

The Hall is believed to be eliminating the senior category so there is no emotional bias toward trying to select a player, say, in his final year as a modern-era candidate, before he disappears into the so-called senior category abyss.

That abyss, by the way, has spit out 19 seniors being selected to the Hall in the last seven years. So this new approach is like the proverbial pendulum swinging away from a concentration on senior candidates being selected.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

The Hall intends to have a coach and contributor subcommittee each consisting of 11 voting selectors and three alternates. Those will consist of some current selectors not chosen among the overall 28.

Those committees will put forward one coach and one contributor to be considered as candidates by the greater group of selectors.

A contributor, by the way, is someone who added to the game outside of playing or coaching. So broadcasters, owners, executives, commissioners and others are eligible. If contributors also played, coached, or served as an executive, their whole body of work will be considered.

Every year the Hall expects to consider 13 players, one coach and one contributor as its candidates.

The Hall of Fame says its class sizes will range from three to seven inductees every year. The typical number of enshrinees is more likely to be five or six because of the math involved.

The reduced number of selectors will meet in person once a year, with the next meeting scheduled for the first week of Feb. 2027.

item.title: Caitlin Clark posts double-double as Team USA opens FIBA Women's World Cup with blowout win over China
item.description: Caitlin Clark posted a double-double with 14 points and 11 assists as Team USA crushed China 94-61 in their FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup opener.
item.content:encoded:
Team USA’s dominance on the world women’s basketball stage continued Friday in Berlin and Caitlin Clark had a lot to do with it.

Clark and Paige Bueckers, both making her senior international debut with Team USA, as well as Rhyne Howard each scored 14 points to help lead the Stars and Stripes past China in blowout fashion to kick off their FIBA Women’s Basketball World Cup play, 94-61.

Clark may have come off the bench for head coach Kara Lawson to start his game – Team USA veteran Chelsea Gray and Jackie Young got the nod – but she played the most minutes of any player on the team (25) and made the most of them.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

She finished the game with a double-double, scoring 14 points on 4-of-9 shooting, including three three-pointers made, with 11 assists.

Also coming off the bench was Bueckers, the Dallas Wings star whom Clark worked well with and China had no answers for. Over 20 minutes of play, Bueckers was highly efficient with her 14 points, going 6-of-9 from the field with four assists. She perhaps could’ve been the team’s leading scorer if she didn’t pick up two quick fouls, with FIBA rules setting a foul-out at five personals compared to the WNBA’s six.

CAITLIN CLARK'S RECORD-BREAKING AUGUST SETS THE STAGE FOR HER FIBA WOMEN'S WORLD CUP DEBUT

Howard was also feeling it when she checked in off the bench, raining in four three-pointers across 18 minutes of work.

Lawson made sure that every single rostered player for Team USA got time on the hardwood on Friday, and they earned it after making quite the statement from start to finish.

Team USA faced this same China team in the 2022 gold-medal game at the FIBA Women’s World Cup, where they came away victorious. They were getting tremendous looks throughout the game, shooting 45% from the field and out-rebounding China, 47-41.

The reason rebounding was a priority in this matchup was due to China’s Han Xu and Zhang Ziyu, who stand at 6-foot-11 and 7-fot-3 respectively. The height gap when they were on the floor was palpable, but it didn’t hurt Team USA as much as it could.

Stellar defense was played by everyone who stepped foot on the court for Team USA, but especially those down low like Napheesa Collier, Angel Reese, Breanna Stewart and more. Team USA tallied nine steals and six blocks, while China shot just 32% from the field and 26% from beyond the arc.

As for rebounding, Reese led the team with nine off the bench, while Stewart had seven with her seven points and Collier picked up six boards.

Finally, young provided some notable scoring early in this game, tallying 12 points on 5-of-11 shooting, while hauling in three rebounds and dishing out three assists.

Team USA will look to carry this momentum into their next matchup against Italy on Sunday at 2:45 p.m. ET.

item.title: Inside a Louisiana courtroom': SEC-LSU legal circus played out like a John Grisham novel in stunning showdown
item.description: Greg Sankey snuck into a Baton Rouge courtroom as the SEC filed a bombshell federal lawsuit against LSU and Lane Kiffin over eligibility rules.
item.content:encoded:
BATON ROUGE, La. — SEC Commissioner Greg Sankey covertly arrived at a Louisiana courtroom Thursday morning more than an hour before the circus was scheduled to begin, just two days before LSU was set to welcome Clemson to "Death Valley.,"

Around the same time Sankey took his seat, Louisiana Attorney General Liz Murrill stepped out of a government vehicle and made her way inside. Before entering, however, she made her allegiance clear.

LSU MIGHT HAVE TO SUE THE SEC IF THIS LEGAL WAR IS EXPEDITED, WHILE DABO SWINNEY IS STAYING IN HIS 'LANE'

"Go Tigers," Murrill, wearing a purple outfit, proclaimed before blasting both the NCAA and SEC

If you didn’t realize the courthouse was just minutes from LSU’s campus, the purple-and-gold atmosphere inside and outside the building made it clear.

SEC LAWYERS, LANE KIFFIN AND DEATH VALLEY: COLLEGE FOOTBALL’S WEEK 1 IS SET FOR FIREWORKS

Television cameras lined the street as reporters waited for everyone connected to the lawsuit to arrive for the highly anticipated showdown.

While nearly everyone involved entered through the front door, Sankey slipped in through a side entrance, avoiding the cameras and reporters hoping to ask him questions.

Why?

The Baton Rouge Sheriff’s Office later released a statement saying Sankey used the side entrance because of threats made against the commissioner before his arrival. Some people associated with the plaintiffs, however, suggested the SEC leader was simply trying to avoid questions.

All of that pregame commotion set the stage for what came next. And to put it mildly, Thursday’s hearing was dramatic.

The conference knew exactly what it was doing Thursday morning.

If you thought Sankey traveled to Baton Rouge empty-handed, you haven’t been following the gamesmanship that unfolded behind the scenes in the days leading up to the hearing.

Just minutes after Greg Sankey took a seat inside the witness box, a noticeable wave of emotions moved through the courtroom.

It was in the early morning hours of Thursday that the Southeastern Conference had initiated a preemptive strike.

The SEC had filed a federal lawsuit in Alabama against LSU, head coach Lane Kiffin and athletic department officials alleging that the school was violating First Amendment rights of the conference just as the hearing in Louisiana was getting underway.

NCAA CREATED THIS MESS, NOW LSU SET TO MAKE DAE’QUAN WRIGHT COLLEGE FOOTBALL’S FIRST NFL RETURNEE

The SEC’s lawsuit alleges that LSU was actively recruiting NFL players to return to college while also preventing the conference from enforcing its rules against professional athletes participating in collegiate sports.

Simply put, the SEC is furious that LSU has challenged the conference’s attempts to enforce its eligibility rules for athletes returning from professional sports.

NCAA HAS NO PLANS TO SURRENDER, AS ELIGIBILITY LAWSUITS FOR 2022 CLASS TURN INTO AN ALL-OUT LEGAL WAR

"Did you authorize the SEC to sue LSU and coach Lane Kiffin?" attorney Tony Clayton asked Sankey.

When asked why the conference took that step, Sankey pointed to the authority of the presidents and chancellors he represents.

"We established our First Amendment right for freedom of association, so that our conference can make decisions and our members can make decisions about membership," Sankey said.

The timing caught the plaintiffs off guard, with attorneys sharing the news amongst them at the table.

Clayton asked Sankey three separate times about the conference suing one of its own members before Judge Will Jorden moved the proceedings along.

Many expected the hearing to take at least an hour before producing any fireworks. Instead, the SEC’s lawsuit created chaos within minutes of Sankey taking the stand.

At the core of the lawsuit were athletes such as Dae’Quan Wright, who spent more than 10 hours inside the crowded courtroom, and their argument that they were placed in this position because of the NCAA’s decision not to grandfather the 2022 class into its new eligibility rules.

The NCAA recently adopted a five-years-to-play-five-seasons model. However, athletes who would otherwise be eligible under the new guidelines were not included.

The dispute has become even more complicated because some members of the 2022 class pursued professional opportunities after exhausting their eligibility under the previous system.

One of the central issues discussed Thursday was why the SEC created new guidelines in late August prohibiting athletes who had pursued professional careers from receiving another season of eligibility.

The argument against allowing professional athletes to return to college is easy to understand.

Most college sports fans would likely agree that a player who has signed with a professional team or participated in a professional training camp should not be allowed to return to the college ranks.

However, Clayton used the timing of the SEC’s new guidelines to attack the conference’s position. He questioned whether the rules were created in response to Judge Jorden’s initial temporary restraining order in the case.

"That was not re-establishing the rule," Greg Sankey said about the SEC's meeting just over 10 days ago in Brimingham. "The rule was the same rule before and after. The rule was there when I arrived in 2002...What was issued in the memo was consistent with the clarity that was understood by our sixteen universities, and if you have an individual on your roster under that policy, here's the accountability that will be applied."

Most people would agree that the SEC’s policy came in response to the series of court orders allowing athletes with professional experience to return to college sports. The Big Ten had already issued similar guidelines before the SEC followed suit.

But after listening to Jorden’s arguments before he granted the athletes an injunction, it was clear there was an undercurrent of concern that the conferences had coordinated their actions to undermine his initial ruling.

That possibility, however subtle, may have helped drive the legal chaos that unfolded in Baton Rouge just 48 hours before LSU was scheduled to take the field.

Call it Louisiana politics or home-field advantage, but LSU now faces a decision about how to proceed Friday afternoon — a decision that will only heighten the hostile atmosphere around campus throughout the weekend.

Now, everyone is waiting to see whether the Tigers will follow through on the chaotic effort to strengthen their roster before the season begins.

Or, as we now call it in college athletics, another Friday afternoon courtroom decision.

item.title: Deion Sanders takes multiple swipes at his critics after Colorado stuns Georgia Tech
item.description: Deion Sanders declared "I'm back" after the Colorado Buffaloes stunned Georgia Tech 14-13 with a blocked field goal as time expired Thursday.
item.content:encoded:
Let's all hop back in a time machine and travel back to 2023, because the Colorado Buffaloes are, apparently, good again.

At least for this week.

Deion Sanders and the Buffs stunned Georgia Tech in Thursday night's opener, 14-13, thanks to a late touchdown and blocked field goal in the waning seconds.

The game marked Sanders' first time back in Atlanta as an FBS head coach, and helped the Buffaloes avenge last year's season-opening loss to Georgia Tech in Colorado.

Of course, it also marked the return of cocky Deion Sanders, which we haven't seen in quite some time. Makes sense, given Colorado has been pretty awful since Shedeur Sanders and Travis Hunter left for the NFL.

COLORADO FOOTBALL OPENS PRACTICE TO FANS AND REPORTERS, BUT TREATS IT LIKE A CLASSIFIED PENTAGON BRIEFING

The Buffs went 3-9 last season, including 1-8 in the Big 12, and have completely fallen out of the national spotlight. Remember a few years ago when CU was on ESPN every single week?

Yeah, things have changed ...

That being said, following last night's stunner, Sanders made sure to let the haters know he was allllllll the way back:

Lordy.

"We rushed for 183 (yards), my God. They rushed for 51. I thought we were small?"

"I'm back."

"I think this is the first sellout they had in how long?... I think we had a little something to do with that."

Yeah, I'd say Deion Sanders is fired up today. Haters can hate all they want, but they don't have a leg to stand on today. Colorado went into Georgia Tech — playing in its first sellout home-opener in 20 years — and ripped their hearts out.

All of that came AFTER a tough summer in which the team was ruthlessly mocked for appearing "small" in now-viral pictures from camp.

COLORADO LOOKS LIKE A POP WARNER TEAM

Nobody gave the Buffaloes much of chance — which was fair given how bad they were last season — but they were the better team all night.

Quarterback Julian Lewis finally put it all together on the final drive, throwing an absolute dart with 37 seconds left to give Colorado the lead:

Amazing. This kid couldn't complete a pass to save his life for 3.5 quarters, and then he put together a masterful final drive.

It's what makes college football the best.

The Yellowjackets quickly move down field on their final drive, but Colorado blocked the field goal as time expired to complete the upset.

And, of course, give Coach Prime all the ammunition he needed for the rest of the season.

Welcome back!

(For now).

item.title: Trump commutes sentence for former Philadelphia union official, attorney says
item.description: Former union official John Dougherty's lawyer George Bochetto confirmed to Fox News Digital that President Donald Trump commuted Dougherty's sentence.
item.content:encoded:
President Donald Trump commuted the sentence of John "Johnny Doc" Dougherty, a former union business manager, according to Dougherty's lawyer George Bochetto.

Bochetto confirmed to Fox News Digital during a Friday morning phone call that the president had inked the commutation on Thursday.

He said that Dougherty would be "released any hour now."

The Philadelphia Inquirer reported that the lawyer indicated the move will also release Dougherty from needing to pay around $1.6 million for restitution, and that the man will not face monitoring or house arrest, but will be "a free man."

Regarding those details, Bochetto confirmed to Fox News Digital, "It's all true."

COLORADO GOVERNOR COMMUTES TINA PETERS' SENTENCE AS TRUMP POSTS 'FREE TINA!'

He said the "compassionate release" was "remarkable in its humanity," indicating that it was "equally as remarkable" that a Republican president granted it to the Democratic political figure. 

He said that it demonstrates that "doing the right thing" can be an endeavor that is "bipartisan," noting that he is "so proud" of Trump.

Bochetto added that he is "so happy for John, and particularly" for Dougherty's "gravely ill wife, who will now have her husband by her side." 

Fox News Digital reached out to the White House on Friday.

Dougherty, a former business manager for the International Brotherhood of Electrical Workers Local 98, was sentenced in 2024 to six years in prison.

The U.S. Justice Department said at the time that Dougherty had been sentenced in connection with embezzling funds from the union as well as in connection with payouts provided to a Philadelphia City Council member.

NATION'S LARGEST TEACHERS UNION UNDER FIRE AS CONTROVERSIAL AGENDA PUTS CENTURY-OLD FEDERAL CHARTER AT RISK

"John Dougherty held himself out as Local 98’s biggest booster," then-U.S. Attorney Jacqueline Romero said in a statement. "But while he was backslapping his electricians with one hand, he was ripping them off with the other. He cheated Philadelphians, too, through his corrupt quid pro quo with Bobby Henon."

"Our city and its workers deserve so much better than union bosses and politicians whose true priority is looking out for number one," Romero, an appointee of former President Joe Biden, added at the time. "I want to thank all of the investigators, analysts, prosecutors, and staff who partnered on this case, and, in doing so, stood up for integrity and the rule of law in Philadelphia."

item.title: Coke vs Pepsi: Why Americans are so fiercely loyal to their soda of choice
item.description: A report revealed Classic Coke was the top-selling soda in the U.S. in 2025, accounting for 18.5% of carbonated soft drink sales volume. Studies explain taste differences and brain science.
item.content:encoded:
The rivalry between Coca-Cola and Pepsi has been bubbling for generations, and a person's preference for one soda over the other likely involves a combination of factors.

The differences in the two sodas' ingredients could help reveal why some consumers prefer Coke to Pepsi, or vice versa, according to The Takeout. The outlet reported that Coca-Cola and Pepsi differ somewhat in their formulations. Pepsi contains citric acid, which Coca-Cola does not, and slightly more sugar per 12-ounce serving — about 41 grams to Coke's 39.

"Few consumer products have been part of culture for as long as cola," PepsiCo told Fox News Digital.

Fox News Digital also reached out to Coca-Cola for comment. 

OLD-SCHOOL SODA WENT FROM BEING A TOP BRAND TO NEARLY UNFINDABLE

"People have known these brands for years, share them at meals and celebrations, and have developed strong personal connections along the way," PepsiCo added. "Combine that history with genuine differences in taste, and it's easy to see why the Pepsi-versus-Coke debate still inspires such strong opinions today."

A report by trade publication Beverage Digest revealed that Classic Coke was the top-selling soda in the U.S. in 2025, accounting for 18.5% of carbonated soft drink sales volume, while Dr Pepper held onto second place with an 8.8% share, reported the Atlanta Journal-Constitution.

Pepsi climbed back into third at 8.1% after falling to fourth behind Sprite in 2024. Pepsi ranked second in 2022 and third in 2023, when Dr Pepper edged past it by a fraction of a point.

Sales don't necessarily reflect taste preference, however.

A team of researchers from Baylor College of Medicine studied the Coke and Pepsi preferences of 67 people back in 2004. The scientists gave participants blind taste tests, then scanned their brains during tastings that involved cues such as flashes of light or pictures of a Coke or Pepsi can.

SOME MARRIOTT GUESTS TOUT COKE'S NEW MOVE AS ‘BEST EVER’ WHILE PEPSI LOYALISTS PUSH BACK

The brain scans suggested that seeing the Coke brand influenced participants' preferences and activated areas of the brain associated with memory and executive deliberate decision-making, suggesting that marketing and cultural associations can influence what consumers think tastes better. 

The Pepsi can produced no comparable effect on the participants. The study was small, however.

"Nothing beats the taste of Coca‑Cola," The Coca-Cola Company declares on its website. "Designed to go with everything, the taste of the classic Coca‑Cola has remained unchanged for more than 130 years. Coca‑Cola is inviting the world to celebrate the real magic of humanity."

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

In 1975, Pepsi fired an early shot in what became known as the "cola wars" when it launched what it called the Pepsi Challenge. The campaign invited consumers to sample Pepsi and Coca-Cola blindly and choose which they preferred. Pepsi declared that more people preferred its taste — and years of advertising urged consumers to "let your taste decide" by taking the challenge. 

No single ingredient defines Pepsi's taste, PepsiCo told Fox News Digital.

"Sweetness is one element of Pepsi's flavor profile," the company said. "Pepsi has been formulated to balance sweetness with tartness, bright citrus and spice notes, and crisp carbonation — creating the bold, refreshing taste consumers recognize as uniquely Pepsi."

PepsiCo believes it's a common misconception that people always know exactly which cola they prefer.

"Many have strong assumptions going in, but when Pepsi is put head to head against our competitor in a blind taste test, those assumptions are often challenged," the company said.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

It also said research shows "half of Coke buyers also purchase Pepsi in a given year." Taste is an important part of why people decide which soda to buy, the company said — but it isn't the sole deciding factor.

"Flavor design and complexity play a role in preference, and people can experience and describe taste differently," the company said. 

"But we don't believe cola preference can be explained by ingredients alone. The overall taste experience, personal preferences and the moments associated with a brand all contribute to why someone may prefer one cola over another."

Pepsi revived the Pepsi Challenge in 2025, putting Pepsi Zero Sugar head-to-head against Coke Zero Sugar and distributing more than 1 million samples across 34 markets in 23 states and Washington, D.C.

"We're confident in what happens when people have the opportunity to put assumptions aside and focus on taste alone," Pepsi said.

A December 2025 Pepsi press release said that "Pepsi Zero Sugar won 100% of the Pepsi Challenge national tour markets (including Coke's backyard – Atlanta!), achieving a consumer preference rate exceeding 60% across the U.S."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS

The nutritional differences between Coke and Pepsi are "too small to matter" from a health perspective, Marion Nestle, professor emerita of nutrition, food studies and public health at New York University, told Fox News Digital.

"Both are sugary drinks with way too much sugar for the body to handle easily when consumed as a drink," Nestle said. "Large amounts of sugar in liquid form are absorbed rapidly by the digestive tract, causing insulin to spike and other hormonal changes, none of them beneficial."

An occasional 8-ounce Coke or Pepsi generally isn't a matter of concern, Nestle added.

"It's the larger ones that cause problems, especially when consumed frequently," she said. "Think of these drinks as instant candy."

item.title: Dennis Quaid says LA has to ‘get a little better’ as he embraces Nashville life
item.description: Dennis Quaid reveals his daily life in Nashville after leaving Los Angeles, saying he'd choose Atlanta over LA if he were starting out in acting today.
item.content:encoded:
Dennis Quaid is shedding light on what his day-to-day life in Nashville looks like six years after leaving Los Angeles behind.

"Basically, I play golf," the actor told People. "I love to be around the house here. You get a lot of land and space, but you’re still in an urban environment. I’ve made some really good friends here to spend time with. It’s important and a great place to raise a family."

Quaid and his wife, Laura Savoie, moved to Tennessee in 2020 after living in California for decades. Quaid told the outlet that the connection to the community he found in Nashville makes it feel like home.

He also told the outlet that the entertainment industry in Hollywood has drastically changed since his early days as an actor.

'80S POP STAR TIFFANY EMBRACES QUIET NASHVILLE ROUTINE AFTER LEAVING CALIFORNIA BEHIND FOR GOOD

"It used to be if you were auditioning for something, you’d go to an office. You’d go in and there would be five people dressed just like you, all up for the same part, waiting for time to read. You met a lot of people that way and that’s where a community was formed," Quaid told the outlet.

He explained that the system has changed and actors are now largely sending in self-taped auditions, which has left him yearning for the sense of community he once felt.

PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE

"Now everybody puts something on tape in their room and sends it in. You don’t have this feeling of community over that," Quaid said.

GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE

"The Parent Trap" star told the outlet that if he was just breaking into acting, he would not put down roots in California at all. "If I was an actor starting out, I wouldn’t go to LA I would go to Atlanta," Quaid said, referring to the accessibility of production studios in the south.

Although Quaid is calling Tennessee home for now, he hasn't completely closed the door on California.

"I might be open to going back to LA later on. I moved before the fires and everything, but I just think things have got to get a little better there," he said, adding, "And it’s so nice here in Tennessee. It’s soft, and it’s a real feeling of community."

In Quaid's six years living in Tennessee, he has learned that there is much more to Nashville than just country music.

"It’s not a one-horse town. It’s not just music, although, like 75 percent of all music in the United States, no matter what genre it is either, not just country is done right here in Nashville," he said.

The actor concluded, "They have so many other industries, and it’s also booming, but it’s still holding its character. I think because it’s not just people from California. There’s people from New York and Chicago and really all over that are coming to live in Nashville."

item.title: Trapped Nepal workers pulled alive from tunnel 9 days after deadly flooding, raising hope for more rescues
item.description: Two workers were pulled alive from a Nepal hydropower tunnel nine days after catastrophic floods, and one rescued man says more people are trapped inside.
item.content:encoded:
Rescue teams in Nepal pulled two workers alive from a hydropower tunnel nine days after catastrophic floods swept through the country, leaving more than 1,000 people dead and thousands more missing.

Nepalese lawmaker Shri Ram Neupane told The Associated Press that searchers first heard men's voices in the tunnel on Friday morning. Images distributed by the Nepal Army showed a rescuer carrying one of the workers on his back while soldiers on either side helped.

The breakthrough has raised hopes that the dozens of others believed to be trapped will be rescued. One of the rescued men said more people are alive inside the tunnel, according to Brig. Gen. Raja Ram Basnet, who said the search is ongoing.

SON REALIZES MISSING AMERICAN DAD WAS IN PATH OF NEPAL DISASTER AFTER WATCHING VIRAL VIDEO

"I can’t explain what we are feeling at the moment. We are just grateful to God," Amir Maharjan, the brother of one of those rescued, told the AP.

Both men were flown to a hospital in Kathmandu, and one of them was in critical condition, the AP reported, citing a statement from the prime minister's office.

Officials identified them as a mechanical foreman and a mechanical supervisor at the Trishuli 3A plant.

TERRIFYING VIDEO CAPTURES PEOPLE FLEEING INCOMING MUDSLIDE AT NEPAL-CHINA BORDER

The AP reported that about 115 people are believed to remain trapped in the Trishuli 3A tunnel alone, citing the Independent Power Producers Association of Nepal.

In total, authorities say there are about 900 workers missing from 12 hydropower plants in Nepal, with about 500 of them believed to be trapped in tunnels.

Nepal’s Communication Minister Bikram Timilsina wrote on his Facebook page that officials "are waiting for the rescue of more and more people."

"A heartfelt thank you to everyone who worked tirelessly day and night to rescue two people alive!" Timilsina added.

The AP reported that at least 1,287 people have been killed and more than 5,000 remain missing after the Aug. 26 floods, which scientists believe were likely triggered by a glacier collapse.

China said on Wednesday that on the Tibet side of the border, 21 people were killed and 541 are missing.

Nepal's disaster agency chief told Reuters on Friday that the flooding has likely caused at least 387.5 billion Nepalese rupees (about $2.5 billion) in damage to infrastructure and property.

The Associated Press and Reuters contributed to this report.

item.title: Former Trump Cabinet official had 'inappropriately close' relationship with bodyguard, IG finds
item.description: Lori Chavez-DeRemer allegedly ordered a security agent to throw cash at a stripper during an Oregon trip, a Department of Labor OIG report says.
item.content:encoded:
Former Labor Secretary Lori Chavez-DeRemer allegedly had an inappropriate relationship with her bodyguard and created a hostile work environment for her subordinates, according to a Thursday report from the Department of Labor's (DOL's) Office of the Inspector General (OIG).

The report cites one incident in which Chavez-DeRemer allegedly ordered a member of her security detail to throw cash at a stripper.

Chavez-DeRemer, who resigned her position in April, had been under investigation after the OIG received an anonymous complaint in January. That complaint alleged Chavez-DeRemer's inappropriate relationship with the assistant special agent-in-charge (ASAIC) of her department's Division of Protective Operations (DPO), who the report did not name.

TRUMP TAPS ACTING LABOR SECRETARY KEITH SONDERLING FOR PERMANENT ROLE PENDING SENATE CONFIRMATION

The complaint also alleged that Chavez-DeRemer, her chief of staff, Jihun Han, and deputy chief of staff, Rebecca Wright, created a hostile work environment and regularly drank alcohol on DOL property and during work hours.

The OIG interviewed 38 witnesses who described the DOL work environment as "toxic, intimidating and humiliating." The witnesses reported that Chavez-DeRemer, Han and Wright "openly discussed employee performance matters in the presence of other staff, including details of performance-related meetings and whether those employees had cried during the meetings."

HIGH-RANKING DHS OFFICIAL SIDELINED OVER ALLEGATIONS OF 'SUGAR DADDY' RELATIONSHIP, LUXE GIFTS AND DRUG USE

Witnesses also told the OIG that Chavez-DeRemer's alleged relationship with the ASAIC also contributed to the hostile work environment.

During an April trip to Oregon, the ASAIC complied with Chavez-DeRemer's request to make an unplanned, off-the-record stop at "an establishment that was determined upon entry to feature partially nude dancers," according to the report.

The ASAIC assigned Chavez-DeRemer's driver to enter the establishment with her, and, according to the report, she handed the driver a stack of cash and instructed him to give it to one of the dancers. When the driver refused, the ASAIC instructed him to comply.

"Chavez-DeRemer then took additional money from her purse and asked the agent to drop the bills one by one onto the partially nude woman. The agent again hesitated and sought intervention from ASAIC 1, who told him to follow Chavez-DeRemer's instructions," according to the report.

The complaint and subsequent investigation also determined that the ASAIC's alleged inappropriate relationship with the former labor secretary, who is married, affected his job performance.

"ASAIC 1 allegedly focused on his interactions with Chavez-DeRemer, monitored her interactions with other agents, and reduced the presence of other DPO personnel to create opportunities to be alone with her, resulting in reduced protective coverage for the Secretary," the report read.

COURT FILINGS REVEAL KYRSTEN SINEMA HAD SEX MULTIPLE TIMES WITH MARRIED BODYGUARD WHILE SERVING AS SENATOR

The pair reportedly grew immediately close upon Chavez-DeRemer's arrival at the department in March 2025, communicating often through the encrypted messaging app Signal in off-duty hours and about non-operational subjects.

Another witness described observing Chavez-DeRemer massaging the ASAIC's shoulders in a car after he had finished a driving shift. When she asked if he was tired, he allegedly responded that he was "solid as a rock," and the pair both laughed.

"The witness interpreted the comment as sexual innuendo," the report read.

MARRIED FEDERAL JUDGE REPEATEDLY HAD COURTHOUSE SEX WITH LAW ENFORCEMENT OFFICER, COMPLAINT ALLEGES

Other witnesses described the pair walking arm in arm after leaving an event at Secretary of Agriculture Brooke Rollins' home. After opening the investigation, the OIG surveilled Chavez-Deremer's Washington, D.C., home and found the ASAIC entering her residence through a back door on repeated occasions.

FEDERAL JUDGE WHO HAD SEX IN CHAMBERS APOLOGIZES TO FORMER CLERK AS IMPEACHMENT PUSH RAMPS UP

However, the SAIC did not escalate beyond this recommendation for fear she herself would be terminated.

"ASAIC 1 declined the suggestion to take leave and agreed that the SAIC taking action to limit his travel with Chavez-DeRemer could result in the SAIC’s removal," the report read.

TWO TAMPA POLICE OFFICERS RESIGN AFTER INVESTIGATION INTO ALLEGATIONS THEY SLEPT WITH A 911 DISPATCHER ON DUTY

When the SAIC told ASAIC in a text message that she would reassign him to another team he replied, "lol. Don't do that."

item.title: University pays professor $600K after being punished for parodying land acknowledgments
item.description: Stuart Reges parodied the University of Washington's land acknowledgment on his syllabus, triggering censorship and a nearly yearlong investigation.
item.content:encoded:
The University of Washington has paid a professor $600,000 after punishing him for parodying a land acknowledgment in his syllabus.

Stuart Reges, a non-tenured computer science and engineering teaching professor at the university, said in his complaint that in September 2020, university officials encouraged professors (but did not require) to include the university's land acknowledgment statement in their class syllabus. Land acknowledgments are statements commonly used by universities and public institutions to recognize Native American tribes as the original inhabitants of the land on which campuses now sit.

Reges parodied the university's land acknowledgment in his Computer Programming II class syllabus in January 2022. Instead of using the university's land acknowledgment, he wrote, "I acknowledge that by the labor theory of property the Coast Salish people can claim historical ownership of almost none of the land currently occupied by the University of Washington."

The Foundation for Individual Rights and Expression (FIRE) said that Reges was punished for his actions.

"UW was not amused. University officials censored Reges’ parody statement from his syllabus and created a competing class, so students could choose not to take a computer science class from Reges. The university also initiated a nearly year-long investigation of Reges under an 'antiharassment policy,'" the organization said.

WOKE STUNT GOES HORRIBLY WRONG AS MICHIGAN DEMS OPEN CONVENTION WITH BRUTAL ‘LAND ACKNOWLEDGMENT’

On Thursday, FIRE announced that Reges' legal battle had concluded with the settlement, following a Ninth Circuit ruling last December in his favor. Under the settlement, the university may take no further action against him over the parody statement.

Reges said in FIRE's press release, "I am deeply grateful to FIRE for this legal victory which will remind public universities that they are obligated to respect the First Amendment rights of their students, faculty, and staff."

He added, "More importantly, I hope that my protest can help reverse a decade-long trend towards ideological conformity in academia and help to convince them that instead of 'protecting’ students from controversial ideas, they should be helping them to learn how to cope with disagreement. Only then can we heal the deep divisions that confront us today."

Gabe Walters, a FIRE attorney, told Fox News Digital: 

"Professor Reges parodied UW's land acknowledgment statement knowing doing so might cause offense, but his deeper purpose was to encourage his colleagues to see beyond their partisan perspectives and consider that others might disagree with them. Epistemic humility is necessary to test ideas, and there's no better place to put ideas to the test than our colleges and universities," Walters said.

CONTROVERSIAL STREAMER HASAN PIKER'S LECTURE AXED BY UNIVERSITY OF WASHINGTON AMID FREE SPEECH QUESTIONS

He added that the case could be better understood by looking at it from the angle of other hot-button issues.

"Consider the flip side of the coin: a state that bans professors from putting indigenous land acknowledgment statements in their syllabi also is putting its thumb improperly on the scale of public debate, and as a non-partisan organization dedicated to the freedom of speech and academic freedom, FIRE also would represent the hypothetical professor who wants to include a sincere land acknowledgment on their syllabi but is prohibited from doing so — just as we've challenged Florida's ‘Stop WOKE Act’ and Texas's campus ban on drag performances."

The University of Washington provided the following statement to Fox News Digital:

"The University of Washington maintains that we acted appropriately, and this settlement is in no way an admission of any wrongdoing. Given the Ninth Circuit’s 2-1 decision overturning the federal district court’s decision in favor of the University, a settlement agreement was the most reasonable option due to the attorney fees and costs that would have resulted from the Ninth’s Circuit’s decision. Prof. Reges has retained his faculty position and continued teaching throughout this process, and his status with the UW remains unchanged."

Fox News' Kristine Parks contributed to this report.

item.title: Trump is dismantling Iran’s war machine, but America still needs an endgame
item.description: Iran exploited U.S. fears of escalation for decades, but Trump's military pressure campaign is finally making asymmetry work both directions.
item.content:encoded:
For nearly half a century, the Islamic Republic of Iran taught Washington to fear confrontation more than Tehran feared attacking American interests. The regime sponsored terrorism, armed proxies, threatened international shipping and targeted U.S. forces while exploiting American fears of "escalation." President Donald Trump has begun to reverse that equation.

The latest strikes matter not simply because Iranian radar, air defenses and maritime assets have been destroyed, but because Washington is imposing a principle Tehran understands: aggression will expose and diminish its military power. For a theocracy that built regional influence by convincing adversaries that retaliation was more dangerous than accommodation, this fundamentally changes the balance of fear.

The latest confrontation in the Persian Gulf illustrates that change. U.S. Central Command said its Sept. 1 operation struck Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) air defenses, radar systems, maritime assets, mine-laying capabilities and communications sites after attempted Iranian attacks on commercial shipping and U.S. service members. Tehran responded with missiles and drones aimed toward Jordan, Kuwait and Bahrain.

TRUMP RETALIATES AFTER IRAN ATTACK AS EXPERT WARNS REGIME IS GROWING MORE DANGEROUS

The attacks demonstrate that Iran remains dangerous, but not strategically strong. Possessing missiles capable of inflicting damage is not the same as possessing the power to dictate a conflict’s outcome.
